title: 'Ask the mufti' purity cases
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y7 lesson 20 (Pupil PDF worksheet: 'Ask the mufti' purity cases)
intro: Lesson 20: Taharah: pure water and removing najasah. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Purity comes first
points: Salah is not accepted without purity

panels.title: Which water purifies?
points: Rain, sea, river and tap water purify
Water stays pure unless its colour, taste or smell changes from impurity
Allah sent down pure water from the sky (25:48)

panels.title: Special case: a dog's saliva
points: A clear rule from the Sunnah

questions.q: Muddy rain splashed on my trousers.
questions.a: Fine for salah: mud and rain are not najasah.

questions.q: Tea spilt on my prayer mat.
A cat drank from my water bowl.
questions.a: The water is pure: scholars cite the Sunnah on cats.
Wash the sleeve: blood is najasah; wudu does not remove it.
Wash it seven times, one of them with earth (the Sunnah).

keywords.def: physical impurity, such as urine or blood
a state that needs wudu or ghusl before prayer
water that is pure and purifies

questions.q: Explain the difference between hadath and najasah with an example of each.
questions.a: Hadath is a state (e.g. after using the toilet), removed by wudu or ghusl; najasah is a substance (e.g. urine on clothes), washed away.

questions.q: How many times is a vessel washed after a dog drinks from it?
Answer five 'Ask the mufti' cases on the pupil PDF (e.g. muddy rain on trousers, tea spilt on a prayer mat, a cat drinking from a bowl). Write the ruling and the reason.
questions.a: Rulings with reasons: mud is not najasah; tea is not najasah; a cat's leftover water is pure (scholars cite the Sunnah)

questions.q: Extend: why can't wudu remove najasah?
questions.a: Wudu removes a state; najasah is a substance that must be washed off.

questions.q: Stretch: how does Islam's focus on purity link to health?
questions.a: Washing removes germs; Islam teaches hygiene as worship.

questions.q: Blood drips on your sleeve. What do you need?
questions.a: A) Wash the sleeve. Blood is najasah: wash it off. Wudu and ghusl remove hadath, not a substance.

questions.q: Think again: can you pray in clothes with a drop of urine?
questions.a: No: wash it first; purity of clothes is a condition of salah.
